title: Color in the air
caption: Airglow and the Milky Way over Cerro Paranal, seen from the VISTA site, Chile
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Colorful airglow fills the sky over Cerro Paranal, and the Milky Way arcs across the mountain in the center of the frame. At its top the Very Large Telescope can just about be made out. A trail of dim yellow lights on the ground runs toward the mountain.

Airglow is a faint light in the atmosphere, given off as atoms and molecules combine and release radiation. It shows only where the sky is dark enough for artificial light not to drown it out. That is why it appears so clearly here. ESO's Paranal Observatory lies deep in Chile's Atacama Desert, far from towns, and has some of the darkest skies on Earth.
The photograph was taken by Y. Beletsky from the site of VISTA, ESO's Visible and Infrared Survey Telescope for Astronomy. Airglow was also the subject of the ESOcast 78 video.

understand.summary: This is a night landscape photograph by Y. Beletsky, taken from the VISTA site. The source gives no camera or color details.
understand.eye: Airglow is faint and shows only where the sky is very dark, and the source does not say how the photograph's colors compare with the naked-eye view.

alt: A mountain with a telescope at its summit under a sky tinted with colored airglow and crossed by the Milky Way, with a trail of yellow lights leading toward it.
